summary:
El Hadji Diouf is a Senegalese former winger and forward whose career combined a standout 2002 World Cup with repeated disciplinary controversies. After beginning in France with Sochaux, Rennes and Lens, he joined Liverpool in 2002 following Senegal’s run to the World Cup quarter-finals. He scored twice on his Anfield debut but managed only six goals in 80 Liverpool appearances. A loan move to Bolton in 2004 became permanent the next year, and he later played for Sunderland, Blackburn Rovers, Rangers, Doncaster Rovers, Leeds United and Malaysian club Sabah.

Diouf earned 69 caps and scored 21 goals for Senegal. He was named to the 2002 World Cup All-Star team, helped Senegal reach the African Cup of Nations final that year, and was included in FIFA’s 100 list in 2004. He was twice named African Footballer of the Year.

His career was marked by repeated allegations and charges over spitting incidents, including at Celtic fans in 2003 and Portsmouth’s Arjan de Zeeuw in 2004. He also received suspensions for misconduct.
